$comment: Written reasons for the capabilities catalogue (docs/DSL_CAPABILITIES.html), batch 7 of N, 2026-11-23 (REG-357, owner: do only 20% of the remaining cases, of mixed complexity). One reason per keyword: what need it serves and why a lower rung of the extension ladder (expression, function, flow step, hand-written code) or an existing keyword cannot do it. The reasons state the need, not the evidence counts: the catalogue's own columns show samples, tests and examples and change as the corpus grows, so a count written here would go stale. The batch is every 5th keyword still without a reason, taken within each kind of value (boolean, text, number, choice, list, object, reference) so simple and complex ones are mixed. Key = slot id exactly as the catalogue shows it; the generator refuses a reason for a keyword the schema does not have.

reasons.guidePageRegion.enabled: A guide page may reserve a side area for gadgets, and an area a page does not need should not leave an empty column; the flag shows or hides the region per page, so the layout follows the page's content.
reasons.schemaObject.uniqueItems: A list of tags or product codes must not repeat a value; the flag makes the boundary refuse duplicates before the data reaches any rule, the same way for every caller.
reasons.flowSchedule.tenantScope: A nightly job in an app with several customer accounts must run once per account, each on its own timeline; naming the tenants gives one independent schedule per tenant, and leaving it out runs the flow only for the default tenant.
reasons.presentationMetadata.formPresentation: Some records are quick to edit and suit a pop-up over the list, others need the whole page; one setting on the concept picks which, so the same data is edited the way that fits it without a custom screen.
reasons.concept.invariants: Rules such as a code being unique or an end date falling after the start date must hold for every row however it was written; declaring them on the concept rejects the write that breaks them, which a check inside one screen or one flow cannot promise for the other paths.
reasons.flowStep.else: A branch needs a second path for when its condition is false, such as sending a rejection notice; the else list holds those steps, so the whole decision stays in one place in the flow.
reasons.pack:events: A pack that offers a reusable feature, such as invoicing, must bring the events that feature raises; the pack lists them, declared or referenced from a model file, so installing it brings the events along instead of each app declaring them again.
reasons.panelLayout.fields: A table or form panel must show certain fields in a certain order; the list names them in order, so the author decides the layout and not the order the concept happens to declare its fields.
reasons.root:experiences: A warehouse worker on a phone and an office manager on a desktop should not land in the same place; each experience says which roles it is for and which device, and the first match wins, so who lands where is decided in the model and not in login code.
reasons.flowStep.timeout: A flow that waits for a person or a payment must not wait forever; the deadline in seconds counts from the moment the step parks and survives a restart, after which the flow continues into its timeout steps, which a timer outside the flow would lose on restart.
reasons.schemaObject.precision: A price needs a fixed number of digits; stating the total digits of a decimal makes the database column and the check at the boundary agree, so no rounding surprise appears later.
reasons.flowStep.params: A step that runs a stored query often needs values from the flow, such as the customer id; the params name each query parameter and what feeds it, a reference to flow state or a small expression, so one query serves many callers instead of one copy each.
reasons.pack:signature: A pack downloaded from a catalogue could be altered on the way; the signature signs the pack's content digest with a key pair, so an installer can prove the content is what its publisher released, which no expression or flow can establish about downloaded content.
reasons.conversion.match: When a conversion fills a field by looking a value up in another concept, for example mapping an old country name to its new id, it must say how the source row is found; the match block names that key, so the migration needs no hand-written join.
reasons.guidePageRegions.left: A guide page's left area, often a menu or help, is a region of its own; this holds the settings for that region only, so the left and right areas can differ without sharing one setting.
reasons.aggregateCollectionLookupField.name: A lookup shows a value from another query on every line, such as the product name on an order line; the name is the key under which that value is attached to each loaded row, and it is never stored, so display data does not leak into the saved data.
reasons.autoPanelSurface.panel: A generated screen is right for most cases and wrong for one; naming a hand-declared panel replaces just that generated surface and every link to the surface follows it, so the author keeps all the other generated screens.
reasons.concept.specializes: A team that needs a concept like a pack's Customer but with extra fields should start from that base and add to it, instead of copying it and losing every later fix; the base is pinned to a pack version, so an upgrade is a deliberate step.
reasons.documentBand.collection: A printed invoice has a header and a table of lines; a line-items band must say which collection of the aggregate it prints and a header band must not name one, so each band reads the right rows.
reasons.field.name: Every value a concept holds needs one handle that is at once its column, its key in the API and the name rules use; the field's name is that handle, unique inside the concept, so the three never disagree.
reasons.flowStep.event: A flow that announces that something happened, such as an order shipped, must say which declared event it publishes, so other flows and listeners can rely on the event's declared shape and a typo cannot create a new event.
reasons.guidePageGadget.series: A chart of sales by month split by region needs to know which query column splits it into lines; naming the column draws one series per value, so a single query serves several lines.
reasons.inboundDoor.eventName: When a verified delivery arrives from outside, such as a payment confirmation, the app must turn it into one of its own events; the name must be one the model declares, so a flow can start from it and a stranger's payload can never invent a new event.
reasons.pack:firstPublishedVersion: A pack's upgrade chain must start at a known point; the first version ever published is pinned once by the publish command and never typed by hand, so the migration chain and the version checks always start from the same fact.
reasons.panelDataSource.parentDataSource: A screen that shows an order and below it the order's lines is a master and detail; the detail data source names the one it hangs under, so choosing a master row refreshes the details without a script.
reasons.presentationMetadata.defaultGroup: A board view needs one choice field whose members become its columns, such as the status; naming it on the concept picks the columns, and when absent the lifecycle status field is used, so a board needs no custom screen.
reasons.query.name: Screens, panels, flows and agents all call the same query; its name is the one handle they use, unique within the model, so a change to the query happens in one place.
reasons.root:$schema: An editor can offer completion and spot mistakes in the model file when it knows the schema; this optional address tells it which one and has no effect on the generated app.
reasons.transactionUiState.default: A workbench toggle, such as the kind of record being entered, must start on one of its choices; the default seeds the control on load, and when absent the first listed value is used, so a condition on the toggle never sees an undefined choice.
